queue.brief: THE BET — the plaza's midday. Three wide shots on seed 42 (early summer, 10:30/13:25/16:55) show the plaza holding 0–1 people; it is the longest-untouched domain (14 iterations). Step one, before building: count plaza presence (x 98..112, y 18..46) by hour on HEAD over 10 seeds × 3 summer days and write the histogram into the ledger — that is c127. Step two: give the plaza a midday of its own. Families: the courtyard already has a KID figure (spawnAgent(): a.kind 'kid', a.small, speed 2.6+, drawn by drawPerson(), named 'a child, running about') that never leaves the courtyard. Build spawnFamilyAgent() — its OWN source under its own cap (FAM_CAP 2, a window ~10:00–17:00 on dry days with daylight > 0.35, rate floored so a summer day sees 3–5 families; never a share of eastCap/laneCap), entering by EAST_GATE_A (and a share by the quay, EAST_GATE_Q). The parent takes a PLAZA_BENCHES seat or the fountain stand (spawnEastAgent's plaza branch has both); the child is a FOLLOWER of the parent by the follower law (re-target off the LEADER several times a second, catch-up scaled to the gap) but with a lead of its own: loops on the roundel, and runs AT the plaza's birds. The plaza has no birds unbidden — updateWildlife lands birds[] on the courtyard lawn and the lane only — so give the plaza a landing band of pigeons on the paving (the 'scare' rule at 4.5 cells already puts a hopping bird up when anyone comes near; the child triggers it, the flush is the payoff). The child returns to the parent's side between runs and the pair leave together, retracing. personName: 'a child, chasing the pigeons' / 'someone on a bench, watching a child'. A 150–300-line diff is expected and welcome: source, follower with a lead, pigeon band, two names, one announce line, __entities role. No R() in draw; every new spawn draw on the family's own roll.
queue.successLooksLike: probes/plaza-midday.mjs, 10 seeds × 3 summer days: plaza presence at 12:00 rises from HEAD's median 0 to 2–4; at least one child-triggered bird flush per family visit; the child never further than 6 cells from the parent for more than 3 s; families 3–5 per summer day, 0 in rain and after dark; census PASS (reshuffle only); the pair leave together. shots/b90-plaza-noon.png shows a small figure mid-run and birds in the air on the roundel; the wide shot at 13:25 on seed 42 is no longer an empty plaza.
queue.avoid: Do not widen eastCap or the spawnEastAgent plaza share (0.32) — the WATCH note says that budget is already shared seven ways; a family is its own source. Do not route families through the courtyard's spawnAgent(). Do not let the child's runs cross the fountain basin (crumbSpot's keep box) or the roundel's tree pits. The kid speed (2.6–3.6) with a follower re-target can trip the motion gate's median rule — compare the worst step against HEAD's kids on the lawn before calling it a bug.

queue.brief: An autumn bonfire on the allotments. The block runs a full year (harvest, fallow, dig weather, cabbages) and autumn is its emptiest season on screen: leaves fall, litter lies, nothing burns. On dry, calm autumn afternoons (leafFallF() > 0.3, !raining, wetF() < 0.4, windF() < 0.5, roughly 1 day in 3 by hash(day, k) — histogram the predicate before choosing k) a holder lights a heap on ONE fixed bare cell of the block, chosen off the grid clear of the timber fence, the shed, the POND and every plot lattice cell (read fallowPlots()' lattice; do not re-derive it). fireF 0..1 rate-capped: kindles over ~1 h sim, burns 3–4 h, dies to embers. A smoke column in drawSmoke()'s own idiom leaning windDir()·windF(); a holder (spawnAllotAgent()'s a.dig shape: sendToPlot to the fire cell, 'stand' with a fork, a.tend) who feeds it and leaves when it dies; litter[] within 3 cells consumed as it burns; an ember glow after dark in a screen pass AFTER applyLight (the night-colour law), visible from the wide shot. Named: 'the bonfire, smoking' / 'the bonfire, down to embers' / 'an allotment holder, feeding the bonfire'; one announce line at kindling. Snow or rain arriving puts it out (fireF target 0).
queue.successLooksLike: probes/bonfire-year.mjs, 8 seeds × 26 days: fires on 25–40% of autumn days, 0 in summer, 0 in rain or wind > 0.5; a holder stands at it on every fire; litter within 3 cells falls to 0 while it burns; the glow is visible at 21:00 in a shots/b91-bonfire-night.png crop and the smoke leans the same way as the chimneys in the same frame; census PASS (reshuffle only); filmstrip 0 POP at kindling. ~80–140 lines.
queue.avoid: Not a new tile and not a structure — one cell, one item, drawn live; do not move the census baseline. Do not put it on a plot (the lattice is harvest territory) or against the fence. No R() in the draw; the day's fire is a hash. Do not let the holder's 'stand' block ALLEY_Y.

queue.brief: The linden's shade is a PLACE nobody reads. The tree's shadow is an ellipse drawn once per frame (centre CX + sunX·1.6·shOffset(), CY + 1.2; radii treeR·0.95·shSpread() by treeR·0.8·shSpread()) and no rule consults it — the picnic pair pick a blanket spot at r 9–12 by R() alone, the napper lies at r 2.6 regardless, and the sundial (c124) sits inside it all day at maturity. Step one: count courtyard presence by kind (kid, napper, picnic, sitter, gardener) at 10/13/16 h on HEAD over 10 seeds × 3 summer days and write it into the ledger — at 13:25 on seed 42 the lawn shows none of them (c135). Step two: ONE predicate inLindenShade(x, y) that the draw and the choices both read (one predicate, one definition). Consumers: the picnic pair choose their blanket spot INSIDE the shade when warmth > 0.65 and shadowF() > 0.5 (hot sun), OUTSIDE it when warmth < 0.45 (cool sun), by R() within the chosen set — no new draws in the branch that already draws; the napper's line and personName say 'in the shade of the linden' / 'out in the sun'; sundialName() says 'the sundial, in the linden's shade' when the crown is out and the dial is inside the ellipse. If step one shows the lawn under 2 people at a summer noon on the median seed, say so with the numbers and stop short of retuning capacity — that is the next manager's call, not this brief's.
queue.successLooksLike: probes/shade.mjs, 10 seeds × 3 days at warmth 0.8 vs 0.35: blanket spots inside the ellipse ≥ 80% on hot days, ≤ 20% on cool days, measured at the CHOICE; the sundial's name flips with the crown (bare in winter → no 'shade'); census PASS with only the reshuffle the picnic's spot draw already owns; canvas IDENTICAL to HEAD when inLindenShade is forced false over the run. The ledger carries the courtyard presence histogram.
queue.avoid: Do not move BENCH_SPOTS — all four are 26+ cells from the tree and never in its shade; the shade's consumers are the lawn kinds. Do not thin the tree's shadow to expose the sundial. Do not retune capacity or the spawn shares in this brief.

queue.brief: The punt to the eyot (c128). The island is the run's newest place and nobody can stand on it: the only way onto it is by water from the JETTY (128.4, 35; onJetty()), where overDeck()'s jetty visitors already stand for a while (a.stop at JETTY.x − 1.3). Count them first on HEAD (10 seeds × 3 summer days: how many jetty stands per day, how long). Then: ONE punt moored at the jetty; in daylight, calm (windF < 0.5) and dry, a jetty visitor whose dwell allows it (priced at the CHOICE against their retire: the trip is ~1 h sim each way plus a stay) steps aboard, poles to the eyot's EAST shore (eyotShore; the channel and the rowboat's lane x 116.5–121.5 are never entered — the crossing runs x ≈ 127 → 126.2, rows 35 → 42, south of the deck rows 30..32), stands under the willow for 1–2 h sim (a.eyot; named 'someone on the eyot, under the willow'), poles back, and resumes their retrace. The punt is two draw items in the rowboat's idiom (drawBoat is the rowboat's: give the punt its own, hull + pole + figure), never under the deck; while it is out the mooring is empty. Swans already keep off the turf (offEyot) — make sure the punt's landing does not put a swan or a nesting duck ON the shore cell it lands at (the 0.9-cell law). __entities takes the punt and the a.eyot stander; one announce line as it pushes off.
